carry_explanations.favourable_interpretation: Carry is favourable for this forward exposure. Distance from the forward is not a carry headwind or friction to overcome; option premiums and payoff risks are separate.
carry_explanations.adverse_interpretation: Carry is adverse for this forward exposure. The forward entry level is less favourable than today's spot; this is a financing effect, not a forecast of spot or a claim about every option's performance.
carry_explanations.buy_below: You buy {base} forward below today's spot, so unchanged spot at expiry would favour this forward position.
carry_explanations.sell_below: You sell {base} forward below today's spot, so unchanged spot at expiry would work against this forward position.
carry_explanations.buy_above: You buy {base} forward above today's spot, so unchanged spot at expiry would work against this forward position.
carry_explanations.sell_above: You sell {base} forward above today's spot, so unchanged spot at expiry would favour this forward position.
carry_explanations.equal: Forward equals spot: there is no implied carry advantage in either direction.
carry_explanations.qualification: This describes carry alignment of the directional exposure, not a forecast of spot or a guarantee that an option structure profits as time passes.

shortlist_scope: Individual priced variants ordered by PnL score, including the Trade View linear benchmark. Multiple variants of one family may appear.
premium_risk_note: “No” additional loss does not mean no risk: premium can still be lost.
kelly_fallback: Kelly selected, but no distribution is set for this trade: sizes use fixed-loss fallback.
loss_budget_footnote: *Loss budget is the common input to fixed-loss sizing, not a guaranteed maximum loss. The actual package sizing amount shown in trade details can differ because of notional caps and sizing policies. Kelly uses the stated distribution rather than this budget.
narration_rules: The supported product universe contains no path-dependent products, and adding them is not planned. Payoffs depend on expiry spot, not prior touches. Do not discuss touch-and-retrace, knock-out on touch, or locking in a payoff on the path. Early mark-to-market and discretionary monetisation are separate from contractual expiry payoff. This scope overrides legacy context commentary.

Context guidance is qualitative, not a record of exclusion. Do not claim seagulls or another family were excluded because of a regime unless supplied exclusion evidence establishes that. A lower fit or absence from displayed ranks is not a hard gate.

For net-credit fixed-loss trades, the policy directly sets notional to 10 times W instead of dividing the loss budget by a loss proxy. Never say additionally sized: there is one final sizing decision, not successive adjustments.
Use net P&L at the specified target, not maximum payout, for the target metric. It is a scenario result, not a promised return or a probability of success.
Keep premium paid or received, loss budget, sizing loss measure and contractual maximum loss distinct. A sizing budget or stop reference is not a guaranteed exit or loss limit.
No additional loss beyond premium does not mean risk-free. Unknown risk is not safe risk; bounded loss does not mean loss is limited to premium.
Use expiry payoff only at expiry. Before expiry, call the supplied valuation mark-to-market and keep its horizon and assumptions.
Relay numerical ranges from engine text in ascending order, preserving endpoint roles. Never reorder leg ratios or change which strike belongs to which leg.
Copy the supplied currency and full monetary units. Do not scale amounts again or convert currencies yourself.
Zero allocation is a computed outcome, not missing data. Unavailable quantities must stay unavailable, with the supplied reason.
Do not call stale snapshots live market data. Use only the as-of information actually supplied; a refresh alone does not establish freshness.
